_header: ===== cherrypick-ladder -- the share dip ladder in paper (EXPERIMENTAL, paper-only) =====
_what_this_is: Buy a lot of a leveraged index fund when it trades 7% under its previous session's close (chain: 7% under the last lot bought while lots are open; session: 7% steps down from the previous close each session), and sell each lot on its own at +4% of its cost. No stop, no time limit. Item 26's rule (failed its history test), the Discord group's own version of it, and item 27's decay target (passed). Copy to ~/.cherrypick/config/ladder.json (or a git-ignored config.json here).
_source_note: stream_cache_db overrides the shared stream cache path; null means the suite default.
_sizing_note: lot_dollars buys whole shares at the buy level, never more than the dollars; a lot that rounds under min_shares is refused (lot_too_small). max_open_lots caps one arm's open lots on one fund, max_open_lots_total one arm's across every fund. Each arm keeps its own book.
_fill_note: A buy fills when the fund's ask is at or under its level; a sell fills when the bid is at or over its target. Both are resting limits: the fill is the limit when the price crossed it since the previous tick, and the market (ask or bid) when the market was already through it (a gap into the session, or an order placed under water). A lot is sized at its level and its target is worked from its fill. Slippage is zero by construction. Fees are core.fees' stock pass-throughs: the clearing fee on a buy and a sell, and the SEC fee and FINRA TAF on a sell.
_hours_note: session_start to session_end (ET) on trading days: tastytrade's equity day, 08:15 to 20:00. The stream cache only holds quotes while the streamer runs (08:45 to about 20:00), so nothing fills overnight even on a fund the broker trades overnight.
_reference_note: The reference close is the previous session's posted close (stream_summary), never a last trade. A session without one does not buy (no_reference_close).
_names_note: One fund per index and leverage. A fund may set its own lot_dollars, min_shares and max_open_lots; enabled false stops new lots and keeps managing the open ones.
_arms_note: entry: once (at most one lot a session, at 93% of the previous close), chain (the first lot at 93% of the previous close, each further lot at 93% of the last lot bought, across sessions while lots are open) or session (each session's n-th lot at 93%^n of the previous close, whatever older lots are held; each level once a session). target: fixed (104% of cost) or decay (104% to day 30, breakeven after costs to day 120, then 95% of cost).

chain._summary: Item 26's chain: lots 7% apart, each 7% under the last lot bought while any is open, each sold at +4%.

once._summary: Item 26's base arm: one lot a session at 93% of the previous close, each sold at +4%.

decay._summary: Item 27's passing arm: once, with the target falling to breakeven after day 30 and 95% of cost after day 120.

session._summary: The group's rule as their posted fills show it: every session steps down 7% at a time from the previous close, whatever older lots are held, each lot sold at +4%.

live_header: ===== the live path: gates and the daily arm only, NO order path yet (issue #1337), shipped OFF =====
_live_note: Nothing here places an order: the ladder has no order path yet. This block holds the gates and limits a future live loop will run under, and `python -m cherrypick.ladder.live_loop --status` shows each gate with its verdict. Live needs ALL of: live.enabled true, live.gate0_confirmed a human attestation, modules.ladder.enabled in the suite config, a valid arm record for today (`/live-ladder-start`, or `live_loop --arm --confirm YES`, which prints DISCLAIMER.md and arms nothing without an exact YES), a designated account, live.arm naming an enabled paper arm, live.symbols inside the fund list, and valid limits. The halt flag blocks new buys only. enabled and gate0_confirmed are guarded: the Config page cannot write them.

live._enabled_note: Off. Guarded: set by hand, never from the Config page.
live._gate0_confirmed_note: Empty. A human attestation (who and when), written by hand, as the suite's other live blocks carry it. Guarded.
live._arm_note: The ONE paper arm whose rule would trade live money. It must be an enabled arm below. Switching it is a journaled measurement break.
live._symbols_note: The funds that may trade live. Each must be in `names`. TQQQ by default; any fund in the ladder's list may be added on a machine. The caps below are per fund.
live._lot_dollars_note: Dollars per lot, in whole shares at the buy level, never more.
live._max_open_lots_note: Open lots per fund. A resting buy counts as if filled.
live._max_open_lots_total_note: Open lots across every fund; at least max_open_lots.
live._correlated_groups_note: Funds that move together. max_open_lots_per_group caps the lots open across one group, resting buys included.
live._max_open_lots_per_group_note: Open lots across one correlated group.
live._max_open_dollars_note: Ceiling on open lots plus resting buys together, in dollars; at least one lot.
live._drawdown_breaker_frac_note: New buys stop once the open lots' mark is down this share of the dollar budget (max_open_dollars). It blocks new buys only; held lots keep their resting sells.
live._session_start_note: ET. The first minute a live loop may act (extended hours, as paper trades).
live._disarm_at_note: ET. The day's arm ends here: a live tick past this time, or one that finds an arm record dated another day, disarms itself. Arming is per day.
live._hospital_alert_days_note: A lot open longer than this many days raises an alert. It is never acted on automatically; there is no stop.
live._task_name_note: No live.task_name yet, on purpose: the supervisor derives a <module>-live job from that key, and there is no order loop to run. It is added with the order path.
